Dicen que antes de las cenizas había una: They say that before the ash there was a single light in the world: the **Gran Fragua**. It was a fire that never went out, and everything good came from it: the steel of the plows, the bread of every morning and the first ember of every home. Around the Fragua the fire circle gathered, and around the fire people shared mate, handed out the asado and told stories.
Una noche la Fragua se ahogó en su propi: One night the Fragua choked on its own fire and collapsed. Nobody really knows why. What the fire devoured turned to ash and slag; what it did not devour changed shape, and stayed hungry.
Por eso estamos acá, en el Campamento Ba: That is why we are here, at the Base Camp, with the few who are left. We light this tiny ember every night to remember how it was. You arrived empty-handed, and that is fine: every ember starts small.

Las Praderas del Mate fueron el primer f: The Praderas del Mate were the world's first fire circle: grass so tall a calf could get lost in it, wind heavy with yerba and, in the middle, a king. The **Rey Jabalí** was no ordinary beast: he was the keeper of the first ember, the mate's. When the Fragua fell, he stayed. And from guarding what was no longer there, he came to believe that guarding meant letting no one through.
Vos lo venciste, y eso cambia algo. Al c: You beat him, and that changes something. As he fell he let go of the ember he guarded, and that ember took the shape of an egg. Take care of it: embers raise their young.
Seguí hacia el **Bosque de Cenizas**. Di: Go on toward the **Bosque de Cenizas**. They say there is a forest that has been burning for years without ever going out. And that at night, there, you can hear howling.

Se cuenta que el séptimo hijo varón de u: They say the seventh son of the same house, if born under a bad moon, becomes a lobisón. The **Lobisón Alfa** was the forest keeper: the seventh of seven brothers who looked after these woods generation after generation. When the forest began to burn he did not leave: he stayed putting out embers with his paws, night after night, until the fire got inside him. Today he howls and not even he knows whether he is asking for help or offering it.
Entre los troncos negros queda un solo á: Among the black trunks a single living tree remains, the **Árbol de Vida**. They say the fire does not dare to touch it. They say.
Más allá del bosque la tierra se abre. S: Beyond the forest the earth opens up. These are the **Minas del Yunque**, where the forgers were finishing one last commission when everything came crashing down. A commission nobody wants to name.
El aullido se corta en seco. Por primera: The howl stops short. For the first time in years, the forest does not sound like a cry for help.
El pedido que no se cancela: The order that is never cancelled

The night of the fall there was a pending order, the biggest anyone remembers: an **endless grill**, ordered by someone who haggled over neither the price nor the hurry.
El **Capataz de Hierro** tomó el encargo: The **Capataz de Hierro** took the order with a promise: «The order is never cancelled». And it was not cancelled. The forgers died or left; he kept going. The golems you saw are half-finished grills that rose on their own to carry on the work.
Cuando lo venciste, el taller se quedó e: When you beat him, the workshop fell silent. For the first time in years, nobody was forging anything.
¿De quién era el pedido? Preguntale al H: Whose order was it? Ask the Herrero. He will play dumb; insist.
Baja el martillo, mira alrededor y dice: He lowers his hammer, looks around and says only one thing: «So it was finished?»
Arriba de las minas empiezan los picos d: Above the mines rise the peaks of the **Cordillera del Fuego**: the chimney of the Gran Fragua, where smoke went up and light came down. Someone had to make sure it neither clogged nor overflowed, and that was the **Señor del Volcán**. A job of balance: neither too much fire, nor too little.
La noche de la caída hubo demasiado, y d: The night of the fall there was too much, and ever since the mountain breathes lava and does not remember how to calm down. He was not evil: he was a chimney nobody unclogged. When you beat him the smoke changed color and a warmer air came down, almost kind.
Ya queda poco camino. El **Cráter de la: There is little road left. The **Cráter de la Escoria** is where the Fragua stood. Those who went came back changed, or did not come back.
La montaña exhala. Parece, de golpe, una: The mountain exhales. Suddenly, it looks like an ordinary mountain.

The Gran Fragua stood here, and here the **Soberano de la Escoria** was crowned: the last master forger, who sat on the biggest anvil and refused to get up when the world came crashing down.

That night he had set the table for the whole valley —the forgers coming off their shift, the old folks, the kids— and stepped out for a moment to fetch more firewood, so there would be enough. When he came back, the Fragua had gone out and nobody had sat down.
Nadie sabe por qué cayó. Él cree saberlo: Nobody knows why it fell. He thinks he knows: that if he had not stepped out, none of this would have happened. Since that guilt has nowhere to be set down, he turned it into work. He swore no fire would ever go out again, fed the fire forests, mines and mountains, and ordered an endless grill so he would have something to cook with when they came back. He is still cooking for forty. He is still waiting.
No lo venciste porque fuera malo. Lo ven: You did not beat him because he was evil. You beat him because he could barely hold himself up anymore. You took a coal from him and he let you, not understanding why it did not hurt.

«Yo sabía que no venía nadie. Se lo dije: «I knew nobody was coming. I told him the way you tell a child: "There's enough, Asador. Enough for everyone."»

«Me dijeron que el Herrero durmió toda l: «They told me the Herrero slept through the night», he says, looking at the ember. «That hadn't happened in years.»

In the Fogón, the Asador keeps serving. But this time, before setting a plate down, he stayed looking at it. An instant. Thirty-eight plates on the table.

«Vos otra vez», dice. «Siempre volvés vo: «You again», he says. «It's always you who comes back.»

«Me fui una vez», dijo, casi sin voz. «Y: «I left once», he said, almost voiceless. «And that wasn't why.» He still does not know whether he believes it.
